report_name: Over Half of Mobile Banking Apps Have Critical Flaws, Study Finds

tools.name: Frida
tools.description: A dynamic analysis and instrumentation tool mentioned in the report for hunting vulnerabilities like bypassable biometric checks in mobile applications.

tools.name: objection
tools.description: A runtime mobile exploration toolkit, powered by Frida, mentioned in the report for testing for weaknesses such as bypassing biometric checks.

vulnerabilities.name: Hardcoded Secrets in Mobile Applications
vulnerabilities.description: 20.3% of analyzed mobile banking apps were found to be storing sensitive data like API keys and private certificates directly within the app package, which can be extracted via static analysis.

vulnerabilities.name: Bypassable Biometric Authentication
vulnerabilities.description: 35.1% of Android banking apps had weak implementations of biometric authentication, potentially allowing an attacker with device access to bypass the check and access the banking session.

vulnerabilities.name: Use of Components with Known Vulnerabilities
vulnerabilities.description: 41.1% of analyzed mobile banking apps were built using outdated third-party software libraries with publicly known vulnerabilities, creating a significant software supply chain risk.

identities.name: Mobile Banking Applications
identities.description: A class of 2,686 mobile banking apps from 487 banks across 64 countries, of which over 51% were found by Ostorlab to have high or critical severity vulnerabilities.

indicators.name: Command-Line Scanning for Hardcoded Secrets in Mobile App Packages
indicators.pattern:
title: Scanning for Hardcoded Secrets in Mobile App Packages
id: 2b8a1c3d-f4e5-4b6c-8d9e-0f1a2b3c4d5e
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects the use of command-line tools like 'grep' or 'strings' to search for common secret patterns (api_key, private_key) within mobile application package files (.apk, .ipa).
  This is indicative of static analysis or reverse engineering attempts to find hardcoded credentials, as described in the Ostorlab mobile banking study.
references:
  - https://www.scworld.com/brief/security-assessment-reveals-widespread-vulnerabilities-in-mobile-banking-apps
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-19
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_tools:
    Image|endswith:
      - /grep
      - /strings
  selection_patterns:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'api_key'
      - 'private_key'
      - 'client_secret'
  selection_files:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '.apk'
      - '.ipa'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate security researchers or developers performing static analysis on applications.
indicators.description: Detects command-line tools scanning for hardcoded secrets like 'api_key' in mobile app packages, a method for finding the 'Hardcoded Secrets' vulnerability.

indicators.name: Frida Server Execution for Dynamic Analysis
indicators.pattern:
title: Frida Server Execution Detected
id: 9e8f7d6c-5b4a-4c3d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects the execution of the Frida server on a device. Frida is a dynamic instrumentation toolkit used for reverse engineering and security testing, including bypassing application controls like biometric authentication.
references:
  - https://www.scworld.com/brief/security-assessment-reveals-widespread-vulnerabilities-in-mobile-banking-apps
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-19
tags:
  - attack.t1631
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/frida-server'
    ParentImage|endswith: '/adbd'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate application security testing or development activities.
indicators.description: Detects the execution of the Frida server, a tool used for dynamic analysis and instrumentation which can be used to find and exploit vulnerabilities like bypassable biometrics.

indicators.name: Mobile App Configuration File Access IOC
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Access to Sensitive Mobile App Configuration Files
id: 7c6b5a49-3d2e-4f1c-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b
status: experimental
description: Detects access to mobile application configuration files that may contain hardcoded secrets.
references:
  - https://www.scworld.com/brief/security-assessment-reveals-widespread-vulnerabilities-in-mobile-banking-apps
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-19
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
level: low
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - 'google-services.json'
      - 'Info.plist'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate developer or build server activity.
indicators.description: Detects access to mobile application configuration files like google-services.json and Info.plist, which the report identifies as potential locations for hardcoded secrets.
